# Assignment instructions

Among many unique aspects of the Trump presidency is his use of social media. Trump famously used Twitter to help launch his 2016 campaign for presidency. After his loss in the 2020 election and the riots of January 6th 2021, Trump was banned from Twitter. Because of this, he helped launch a rival social media site called Truth Social. Trump posts frequently on Truth Social regarding a range of topics. You will need your VPN turned on - you can view his posts here: [https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump]()

Imagine yourself to be a social media intern at the White House. You are tasked by Trump to analyze his posts since becoming president to find out which kind of posts generate the most engagement (in this case, your response variable should be `like_count`). He asks you to consider a few factors. One is the the time he posts - does engagement depend on when he posts? Second is the length of the post - does it matter how long it is? You should use the `word_count` variable for this. 

For considering the time of day, you may need to use the `lubridate` library as discussed [here](https://lubridate.tidyverse.org/). You can see the variable definitions [here](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/troykueh/donald-trumps-truth-social-posts-nlp-analysis).

You will need to use all the material we learned in class to:

1.  Think carefully about the sampling frame, what your research expectations and questions are, and how the method of data collection can influence your findings
2.  Interpret summary data
3.  Examine important bi-variate relationships
4.  Construct a high-quality multiple variable regression model of likes and at least the following variables: some measurement of time time and `word_count`.
5.  Interpret this model, including ALL relevant diagnostics and $p$ values.
6.  Propose a plan to Trump about which features of his post generate the most likes.
7.  Also note the limitations of the report and what other data you think Trump should consider before reaching a final conclusion

## Specific requirements

-   Create a new Quarto document in HTML format and name it `Truth Social report.qmd`.
-   Rename the title of your report to `Truth Social report`
-   Add the appropriate date and author information to the header
-   Final report should be between 2000 and 3000 words
    -   Maximum 8 graphs
    -   Maximum 6 tables
-   Suggested structure:
    -   Introduction
    -   Expectations and specific hypotheses
    -   Summary statistics
    -   Regression interpretation
    -   Regression diagnostics
    -   Interpret coefficients
    -   Proposed plan for Trump
    -   Conclusion

## Considerations

Here's a **non-exhaustive** list of things you might want to do:

- Like Determinants: Analyze the relationship between key predictor variables and `like_count`. Explain which features of a Truth post are the most influential in determining the number of views. You should use a multiple regression model to analyze this.

- Adding Additional Variables to the Model: You can create one or several models, but there must be one, final, model that you focus your interpretation on. You can consider more variables than what he requested - a good number might be 2-3 quantitative variables and 2-3 categorical variables.

- Filtering or Subsetting Truth Posts: There may be some type(s) of Truth posts that are not related to the main analysis type, you can consider removing these from the analysis but make a note of why you chose to do that.

- Variable Transformations: Consider applying transformations (e.g., log, square root) to some of the variables if they show non-linear relationship between the predictor and response variable. This could improve the accuracy of your regression model.

- Recommendations: Based on your analysis, provide recommendations to Trump as to what kind of Truth post is likely to generate the most likes. What kind of posts should he focus on?

## Points of emphasis

-   Expectations and specific hypotheses section should include some expectations you develop from finding news articles or studies related to your research question. You should specifically state some hypotheses that seem likely that 1) follow from your literature search and 2) answer the question posed in the Assignment Instructions section.

-   Do not exclude a variable just because it initially does not meet the regression requirements. However, consider carefully whether some variables are actually highly related to another predictor variable -- do not include collinear variables.

-   You should focus your graphs and tables on that illustrating the most important information for drawing your conclusion. Choose your tables carefully such that they convey the key information needed to arrive at your conclusion. Do not make tables and graphs of irrelevant information or points that do not need discussing.

-   Make sure to also interpret the coefficients. You need to interpret the impact of a one unit change in the coefficients on the response variable. You additionally need to examine whether changes in the predictor variables lead to a substantively large or small change in the predictor variable. One way to do this is creating a table of the predictor variables, examining whether a Q1 to Q3 value leads to a large or small change in the response variable. Another way is by the marginal effect plots we have previously used. 

-   Your report should be a polished, quality product that you would be proud to show your boss/employer. No unnecessary printed code, poorly labeled graphs, or strange looking formatting. Use everything you have learned in this class to make a quality final product! Remember, this document is not a formal essay.
